# logfire_gateway_prebuilt_guardrail (Resource)

Manages the targets of an AI Gateway prebuilt guardrail, which applies a Logfire guardrail template such as a PII detector.

~> **Beta:** this resource is backed by a Logfire API in Beta. Its schema and behavior may change in backwards-incompatible ways before general availability.

Requires Growth, Enterprise Cloud, or self-hosted and a token with organization:read_gateway and organization:write_gateway scopes (organization:read and organization:write are also accepted). The organization has one configuration per template. Create adopts a configuration that already exists and replaces its targets. Import accepts the template slug.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Flag email addresses on every endpoint.
resource "logfire_gateway_prebuilt_guardrail" "email_addresses" {
  template_slug = "pii-email"

  targets = [
    { action = "flag" },
  ]
}

# Redact credit card numbers on the support endpoint, and block them on the billing endpoint.
resource "logfire_gateway_prebuilt_guardrail" "credit_cards" {
  template_slug = "financial-credit-card"

  targets = [
    {
      endpoint_slug = logfire_gateway_endpoint.support.slug
      action        = "redact"
    },
    {
      endpoint_slug = logfire_gateway_endpoint.billing.slug
      action        = "block"
    },
  ]
}
```

## Targets

`targets` is the complete set of targets. A change replaces the whole set in one
request. A target without `endpoint_slug` applies to every endpoint, and it
cannot be combined with endpoint targets. Each endpoint can appear in only one
target. Reference an endpoint as `logfire_gateway_endpoint.<name>.slug`, so that
Terraform creates the endpoint first.

Every action other than `observe` needs guardrail enforcement on the
organization plan. Without it, Logfire refuses the apply with a `403` answer
that names the action.

If an endpoint is deleted, Logfire deletes the targets that name it. The next
plan shows the missing targets as a change, and the apply fails while the
endpoint does not exist.

## Endpoint replacement

Logfire also deletes the targets when Terraform replaces an endpoint and keeps
its slug, for example with `terraform apply -replace` or after `terraform taint`.
Terraform plans the guardrail before the replacement, so it plans no change.
After the apply, the new endpoint serves requests without the guardrail. The
next apply adds the targets again.

To replace the guardrail together with the endpoint in the same apply, add
`replace_triggered_by` with the `id` of each endpoint that `targets` names:

```terraform
resource "logfire_gateway_prebuilt_guardrail" "credit_cards" {
  # ...

  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [logfire_gateway_endpoint.support.id]
  }
}
```

The replacement deletes the guardrail and then creates it again. For a short
time during the apply, the guardrail does not apply to any endpoint.

Do not set `create_before_destroy` on this resource. The new resource adopts the
template configuration, and the destroy of the old resource then removes it.

## Samples

`sample_messages` holds the samples that the Logfire UI shows in the guardrail
editor. Samples do not change what the Gateway enforces. If you omit the
attribute, Terraform never changes the stored samples, so samples that someone
saves in the UI stay. Set it to manage the samples from Terraform, or to `[]` to
remove them.

## When changes take effect

A successful apply means that Logfire stored the change and queued a Gateway
configuration refresh. The Gateway applies the change shortly after. It does
not mean that the Gateway already enforces it.

## Templates

Logfire configures each template at most once per organization, so
`template_slug` identifies the resource. Logfire validates the slug, and a
change replaces the resource. Create adopts a template that the organization
already configured, for example in the UI, and replaces its targets. Destroy
removes the template configuration.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `targets` (Attributes Set) Complete set of targets. A change replaces the whole set in one request. A target without `endpoint_slug` has the type `all`. It applies to every endpoint and cannot be combined with other targets. If an endpoint is deleted, Logfire deletes its targets, and the next plan shows them as a change. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--targets))
- `template_slug` (String) Slug of the Logfire guardrail template. Logfire validates the slug. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `sample_messages` (Attributes List) Sample messages that the Logfire UI shows in the guardrail editor. They do not change what the Gateway enforces. If you omit this attribute, Terraform keeps the samples stored in Logfire, including samples set in the UI. Set it to `[]` to remove them. At most 20 messages. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sample_messages))

### Read-Only

- `category` (String) Template category.
- `description` (String) Template description.
- `id` (String) Template slug of the configured guardrail.
- `name` (String) Template name.

<a id="nestedatt--targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targets`

Required:

- `action` (String) What the Gateway does on a match: `observe`, `flag`, `redact`, or `block`. Every action other than `observe` needs a plan with guardrail enforcement.

Optional:

- `endpoint_slug` (String) Slug of the endpoint the target applies to, for example `logfire_gateway_endpoint.default.slug`. Omit it to apply the target to every endpoint.


<a id="nestedatt--sample_messages"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sample_messages`

Required:

- `content` (String) Message text. At most 4000 characters.
- `role` (String) Message role: `system`, `user`, `assistant`, or `tool`.

## Import

Import a configured template by its slug:

```terraform
import {
  to = logfire_gateway_prebuilt_guardrail.email_addresses
  id = "pii-email"
}
```

Or use the command line:

```shell
# Import a configured prebuilt guardrail by its template slug.
terraform import 'logfire_gateway_prebuilt_guardrail.email_addresses' "pii-email"
```
